requested_parts: If Powerstorm grants a Spirit a Repeat of a Power Card that it already paid to play, must that Spirit pay the card’s Energy cost again to use that Repeat?
answers.answer: Yes. Powerstorm requires paying the repeated Power Card’s Energy cost again for each Repeat; the original play payment does not cover it.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

requested_parts: Dahan Enheartened at Terror II or III gives each player Gather and Damage instructions in their chosen land.
Players A and B each choose to Gather one Dahan.
May A Gather, then B Gather, then both deal their Damage
or must one player finish that player's full instructions before the next begins?
answers.answer: Resolve each player’s “each” instructions sequentially: Player A gathers and deals their Damage, then Player B gathers and deals their Damage. One player completes their instructions before the next begins.

evidence.text: Fear effects are not Spirit Powers. For “each player,” one player follows all instructions, then the next; choices can affect anywhere allowed by the card without the player's own Presence or Power Range. Generic Presence/Sacred Site requirements can use any Spirit's; wording explicitly counting each Spirit's own sites is individual. The same piece can be chosen or moved by multiple players unless the card requires different choices. Fear effects last for the turn unless they change the board. For outcome timing, a card containing **only “each” instructions** creates one action per “each” (e.g., per player). A card mixing a global instruction with “each” instructions is one overall action with nested actions per “each”; complete that whole action tree before checking outcomes. [FAQ actions-for-fear-and-event-cards-with-both-each-and-non-each-instructions]

requested_parts: After a primary action and all triggered actions finish, an Invader is still illegally placed.
Do players check victory/defeat with that illegal position first, or correct its position before that check?
Assume a legal destination exists.
answers.answer: Correct the illegal placement before checking victory or defeat. Cleanup happens before the outcome check and is not a Move or other action; it triggers nothing.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

requested_parts: Thunderspeaker has met both a threshold making one of its Innates Fast and a threshold that can affect game state.
Is the Speed-changing threshold handled only as an ordinary effect when resolving that Innate, or applied before checking the phase in which the Innate can be used?
answers.answer: Apply a threshold changing Speed before checking the phase in which the Innate can be used. Thunderspeaker’s met Fast threshold makes the Innate available in Fast.

evidence.text: - Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.

requested_parts: Bringer has used Vengeance of the Dead in a land.
A later action by another Spirit actually destroys a Town there, causing Bringer's Vengeance to trigger.
Is the triggered Damage real because the other Spirit caused the trigger
or does it still follow To Dream a Thousand Deaths?
answers.answer: The triggered Damage still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance of the Dead. Since Bringer used it, the Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit caused the triggering destruction.

evidence.text: - **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. [Core: what-items-are-triggered-actions, .bu6oc8x, .7w4gdth, .7w4gdtj]

requested_parts: A populated land matches both the Ravage card and the Build card this turn.
A Spread of Rampant Green has three Presence in that land and uses Choke the Land with Green to skip its Ravage, destroying one of those Presence.
No other effect changes the land before Build.
Does that payment also skip the later Build
or must Green choose again and destroy another of its Presence there?
Is the remaining Sacred Site sufficient for that second use?
answers.answer: Green must decide again for Build and destroy another Presence to skip it. Starting with three, the first use leaves a two-Presence Sacred Site, enough for the second use; afterward one Presence remains.

evidence.text: - **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there. A later Build needs a fresh decision and another disk: starting with three, Green may skip the Ravage, retain a two-disk Sacred Site, then skip the Build and end with one disk. **Steady Regeneration**'s Healthy/Blighted test refers to the Blight Card, not Blight in the destination land. When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. requested_parts: A Ravage destroys a Dahan.

evidence.text: - **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. Should all 14 be used for that Spirit's setup and later Presence availability

evidence.text: 6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. May one disk be placed in the Ocean of a different island board where Ocean currently has no Presence, without measuring a numeric Range from its existing Presence?

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. Its base Damage would destroy a Town, so that Town is Pushed into an adjacent other Coastal land on the same board.
Tsunami’s threshold later deals Damage in that land.
Counting only nightmare-destruction Fear from that same Town, can it produce that Fear again during this single Tsunami use, or only once?
answers.answer: No. A given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once within one Power use. The Town’s nightmare-destruction Fear is earned at most once during this Tsunami use, even if it is later damaged again after being Pushed.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.
